prompt: A gym chain's membership grew 10% last year, but revenue grew only 2%. Which is the strongest initial hypothesis?

options.text: Churn has likely risen, so the gym is losing paying members.
options.feedback: Membership grew 10%, so the gym isn't losing members overall. The gap is in revenue per member.

options.text: Discounts, cheaper plans, training sales and billing errors likely play a part.
options.feedback: This lists four causes without picking the likeliest, so it doesn't tell you where to look first.

options.text: Growth likely came from discounted plans, cutting revenue per member.
options.feedback: Right. Revenue growing slower than members means revenue per member fell, and new members on cheaper plans is the likeliest reason. I'd compare revenue per member by plan type.

options.text: New gyms are probably opening slower than planned.
options.feedback: Slow openings would hold back members, but members grew 10%. It doesn't explain why revenue lagged.

explanation: The data shows members up 10% but revenue up only 2%, so revenue per member fell about 7%. Likely cause: growth came from discounted plans. To test it, compare revenue per member by plan type and joining date. If new members pay full price, look at existing members downgrading instead.
